children: CoreCivic’s third-quarter revenue rose from a year earlier as higher Residential occupancy and per diem rates, including increased ICE populations, lifted results; Services also benefited from the CSP acquisition. Earnings surged primarily on a $1.77 billion gain from four facility sales, partly offset by related taxes.
¹ Reported as “REVENUE”. ² Reported as “NET INCOME”. ³ Reported as “DILUTED EARNINGS PER SHARE”.
: Segment revenue increased 15.2% to $651.9M; average daily compensated population rose 9.3% to 60,352.
: Average compensated occupancy reached 84.0%, versus 76.7% a year earlier, largely reflecting higher ICE populations and recently activated facilities.
: Four detention facilities sold to DHS for aggregate gross proceeds of about $2.21B; CoreCivic continues to manage them under existing ICE contracts.
: A five-year ICE agreement began August 11; the 1,600-bed facility is expected to start receiving detainees in 4Q 2026, with activation estimated complete in 2Q 2027.
: CSP, acquired April 1, contributed to segment growth; Services net operating income was $9.6M, compared with $1.1M a year earlier.

title: CoreCivic 3Q 2026: Revenue $744.09M, EPS $14.49 — 10-Q Summary
